name: Dispensary Districts 8 Apr 1951
description: The 576 dispensary districts of Ireland at the census of 8 Apr 1951, mapped from the District Electoral Divisions the census report lists for each (CSO Census of Population 1951, Vol. 1, Table 10, which gives each district's DEDs by their 1911 reference numbers, read against the DEDs and acreages of Table 11). The DED map is Phelim Birch's and Paddy Matthews's District Electoral Divisions in force on census day (Connacht 1919, Leinster 1949, Munster 1950, Ulster 1921). Every district carries a grade (confidence) and the reason for it (confidence_reason): A where the printed area equals the sum of its DEDs' areas in Table 11, so the composition is the census's own; B where the composition checks only as part of a group or needed a small adjustment; C where it could not be checked, for the reason given. 567 are graded A and 9 C: Droichead Nua and Kilcullen (Kildare) and Carna, Roundstone No. 1, Lettermore and Oughterard (Galway), which divide DEDs (each placed with the district holding its larger part), and Donegal, Glenties and Tantallan, whose printed areas still follow the DEDs before the County Donegal (DEDs) Order 1946 while Table 11 has the new ones. The city dispensary districts of Dublin, Cork, Limerick and Waterford are not mapped: the census builds them from parts of DEDs and wards, so each county borough is shown as one unit, without a population. A district that crosses a county boundary is shown as one part per county, as the table prints it. Each district carries its census area, population, Table 10 reference numbers and DEDs; quote census_acres rather than the map area, which takes in lakes and estuaries the census leaves out.
